bull_case: Microsoft combines net cash, enormous operating cash flow, recurring enterprise revenue and diversified franchises. Even a severe slowdown would leave substantial internal funding for R&D and essential infrastructure without forced equity issuance.
bear_case: AI infrastructure commitments, long-duration leases and supplier obligations can be large, and capex has risen sharply. A deep cloud slowdown could reduce discretionary buybacks and force capital prioritization even though solvency remains strong.
thesis: Financial survival is exceptionally strong. The frozen balance sheet shows roughly $36.5B net cash and FY2026 OCF of $182.9B, while the company funds large capex, R&D and shareholder returns internally. AI infrastructure commitments increase fixed capital requirements, but current evidence does not indicate external-capital dependence, problematic dilution or material insolvency risk.

evidence.claim: Frozen methodology gives approximately $36.549B of net cash, or about $4.922/share.
evidence.source: Uploaded Microsoft FY2026 Form 10-K / frozen company_context

evidence.claim: FY2026 operating cash flow was $182.935B, providing very large internally generated liquidity.
Cash and short-term investments totaled $76.843B versus current and long-term debt of about $40.294B at June 30, 2026.
Microsoft returned more than $43B to shareholders during FY2026 while simultaneously funding very large AI/datacenter capex.

counterevidence: AI/datacenter growth raises lease, purchase and infrastructure commitments that are not captured by simple net cash alone.
Accelerator refresh cycles can make sustaining capex higher than historical software-era norms.
SBC remains a recurring economic claim even though repurchases offset share-count dilution.
unknowns: Long-run maintenance capex after the AI buildout
Stress-case cloud margin under severe price competition

uncertainties.rationale: SBC is visible and manageable, but AI infrastructure purchase/lease commitments need continued monitoring.

falsifiers: Net cash turns into sustained material net debt while owner FCF remains depressed.
Microsoft requires external equity issuance to fund ordinary AI/cloud growth.
Large off-balance infrastructure commitments become inflexible during a major demand slowdown.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Microsoft funds operations, R&D and major capital investment from very large operating cash flow and retains net cash.
SBC is material but share count remains roughly stable and internal cash flow supports repurchases without external financing dependence.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Net cash, diversified recurring cash flows and $182.9B of FY2026 OCF make financing-driven permanent loss remote relative to the operating opportunity.

key_kpis.name: Net cash / debt
key_kpis.threshold: Remain conservatively financed through the AI buildout

key_kpis.name: Operating cash flow
key_kpis.threshold: Stay well above mandatory investment and financing needs

key_kpis.name: Off-balance infrastructure commitments
key_kpis.threshold: Remain manageable relative to OCF and contracted demand

subscores.rationale: Net cash and enormous internal cash generation provide strong liquidity with modest debt burden.
Diversified recurring franchises allow Microsoft to continue investing through a severe slowdown without forced financing.
Dilution is contained, but AI infrastructure leases and purchase commitments warrant monitoring.
